name: A dialect usage (lugha)
definition: In the books of grammar, a way of speaking of one tribe or group of Arabs that differs from the common usage: 'there are two lughas in it'.
body: The grammarians collected the usages of the tribes, Tamīm, Ḥijāz, Ṭayyiʾ and others, and kept them as lughāt beside the rule. The Ḥijāzīs give mā the work of laysa (mā zaydun qāʾiman), the Tamīmīs do not; and some Arabs put a sign of the plural on a verb before its plural subject, the usage the books call 'the dialect of akalūnī al-barāghīth', after the example 'the fleas ate me'. Al-Zubaydī reports that ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar was the first to build a book on the usage of most Arabs and call the rest lughāt.

examples.text: 'The fleas ate me': the dialect that marks the plural on the verb before a plural subject.
